lessons.titleEn: a small nudge in the right direction
lessons.titleZh: 朝合適方向的一點鼓勵

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A kind comment can be a small nudge in the right direction.
sources.expression: a small nudge in the right direction

brief.meaningEn: A slight encouragement or influence that helps someone move towards a helpful choice or a goal they value.
brief.meaningZh: 一點輕微鼓勵或影響，幫人朝有幫助的選擇或自己重視的目標前進。
brief.grammar: be/give someone a small nudge in the right direction; count noun with a/an article and an optional adjective such as small. This is the noun frame corresponding to the gentle-influence verb nudge someone in a direction.
brief.register: Established encouragement noun image. Right reflects the helpful direction in context, not proof of one universally correct life path.
brief.boundaryZh: 小鼓勵不等於強迫、代做或結果已保證；應交代當事人的目標及自己仍可選甚麼。
brief.misconceptionZh: 別人覺有益未必符合本人需要；可提供線索及邀請，不代他接下承諾。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把輕微支持連到自選下一步，保留當事人決定及未完成部分。

listening.promptZh: 小鼓勵與當事人選擇怎連起來？

options.en: The neighbour’s offer encouraged a first step towards something the speaker already wanted to do.
options.zh: 鄰居的提議，鼓勵說話者朝本來想做的事踏出第一步。

options.en: The neighbour registered the speaker for a gardening course without asking.
options.zh: 鄰居未問便替說話者報了園藝課。

options.en: The speaker had already grown a complete balcony garden before receiving the offer.
options.zh: 收到提議前，說話者已種好整個露台花園。

options.en: The offer led the speaker to give up planting and return the empty pot.
options.zh: 提議令說話者放棄種植，退回空盆。

listening.explanationZh: 提議支持已有種植願望，當事人自行選盆、查起步；不是代報名、已全種好或放棄。
listening.en: I wanted to grow something on the balcony but kept putting it off; my neighbour’s offer of one spare cutting was a small nudge in the right direction, and I chose a pot and asked how to begin.
listening.zh: 我想在露台種些東西，卻一直拖着；鄰居提出給我一枝多出的插枝，是朝合適方向的一點鼓勵，我便選了盆並問怎開始。

reply.promptEn: Why did the neighbour’s offer help you begin?
reply.promptZh: 鄰居的提議為甚麼幫你開始？

options.en: One spare cutting gave me a manageable way to try the planting I had wanted to do.
options.zh: 一枝多出的插枝，讓我可小規模試原想做的種植。

options.en: It was a small nudge in the right direction because it made my first step feel possible.
options.zh: 它令第一步顯得可行，所以是朝合適方向的一點鼓勵。

options.en: The offer supported my interest without choosing a whole course or garden plan for me.
options.zh: 提議支持我的興趣，沒有替我選整個課程或花園計劃。

options.en: I had a concrete starting point and could ask how to look after it.
options.zh: 我有一個具體起點，也可詢問怎照顧。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均說明小而可選的支持，不把鼓勵變替人安排所有步驟。

scene.promptZh: 家人未問你便報了整季課程，要求你必須去，沒有拒絕或改期空間；你想分清這與一點建議。哪句最準確？

options.en: That imposed commitment is more than a small nudge in the right direction; the person’s choice has been removed.
options.zh: 這項被強加的承諾，超出一點鼓勵；當事人的選擇被拿走。

options.en: A whole course chosen without consent is simply a slight optional suggestion.
options.zh: 未經同意選好整季課，只是一項輕微而可選的建議。

options.en: The account says the family offered one question and left the decision entirely open.
options.zh: 敘述說家人只提一個問題，把決定完全留給本人。

scene.explanationZh: 固定承諾且不能拒絕，不是輕微可選的提示；描述沒有把決定留開。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 a small nudge in the right direction 推出？

options.en: A slight influence helps someone towards a useful next step.
options.zh: 一點輕微影響，幫人朝有用的下一步前進。

options.en: The helper may decide every later commitment without consulting the person.
options.zh: 幫忙者可不問本人，便決定之後所有承諾。

options.en: The context should explain why that direction fits the person’s goal.
options.zh: 情境應解釋該方向為何配合當事人目標。

contrast.explanationZh: 小鼓勵不是全面授權，何謂合適也需看本人的目標。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說既然鄰居幫你開始，就應由鄰居替你選全部植物及花費；你只接受一枝插枝。哪句最好？

options.en: It was a small nudge in the right direction, not permission to take over the garden; I still want to choose what I try next.
options.zh: 那是朝合適方向的一點鼓勵，不是接管花園的許可；我仍想自己選下一步試甚麼。

options.en: Accepting the cutting means I have agreed that the neighbour should choose the planting plan.
options.zh: 接受插枝，表示我已同意由鄰居選種植計劃。

options.en: I should ask the neighbour not to offer any more suggestions, even if I could choose whether to use them.
options.zh: 我應請鄰居別再提任何建議，即使可由我選擇是否採用。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可以感謝小幫助，同時保留下一步決定；接受插枝不等於全部授權，自己選擇也不需一概拒絕之後的建議。

speaking.en: Her short question was a small nudge in the right direction, helping me choose an opening without writing the story for me.
speaking.zh: 她的簡短問題是朝合適方向的一點鼓勵，幫我選開場，沒有代我寫故事。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把小提示與代做分開。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你請朋友讀小說草稿，想得到能幫你重想人物動機的問題，而非請他替你寫結尾。你願聽建議，但最後仍想自己決定故事方向。用一至兩句英文直接說明想要哪種回饋。

examples.en: A question about what my character wants could be a small nudge in the right direction. Please help me rethink the motive rather than write the ending for me, so I can choose how the story develops.
examples.zh: 問角色想要甚麼，可能是朝合適方向的一點鼓勵；請幫我重想動機，不代寫結尾，讓我自己選故事怎發展。

examples.en: I would welcome a nudge in the right direction through a question that makes me look again at the character’s choices. I still want to decide the ending myself, rather than ask you to replace my draft with yours.
examples.zh: 我歡迎用問題引我重看角色選擇，給合適方向的一點鼓勵；我仍想自己決定結尾，不是請你用自己的稿取代我的。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以作者身份要求有助思考的問題，保留接受建議與自己決定兩面；不把求回饋當委託朋友代寫。

takeaways.en: The note beside the unfamiliar tool was a gentle nudge in the right direction, prompting him to ask for a demonstration before trying it.
takeaways.zh: 陌生工具旁的便條，是合適方向的輕微提示，促使他先求示範再試。

takeaways.en: Her suggestion was a small nudge in the right direction, but the final choice about joining the group remained mine.
takeaways.zh: 她的建議是合適方向的一點鼓勵，但是否加入小組，最後仍由我選。

sources.sentence: The award was the icing on the cake after months of progress.

brief.meaningEn: An additional pleasure or benefit that makes an already good situation even better.
brief.meaningZh: 令本來已不錯的情況更好的額外樂趣或好處。
brief.grammar: X is/was/would be the icing on the cake; first identify what already makes the situation worthwhile, then the extra benefit.
brief.register: Established food metaphor. The icing is the welcome extra, not the only reason the experience has value.
brief.boundaryZh: 有額外好處不代表主要成果不重要；失去額外獎賞，也未必取消原有價值。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不宜把本來令人失望的情況中唯一勉強可取之處，當作已有美好基礎上的額外好處。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分清主要收穫與錦上添花，按真實結果用肯定或假設語氣。

listening.promptZh: 主要收穫與額外好處是甚麼？

options.en: Completing the story was rewarding in itself, and the public reading added another pleasure.
options.zh: 完成故事本身已有收穫，公開朗讀再添一份喜悅。

options.en: The group began writing only after the village evening had promised to read the story.
options.zh: 村裏晚會答應朗讀後，小組才開始寫作。

options.en: The story remained unfinished, and the reading replaced the need to finish it.
options.zh: 故事仍未完成，朗讀取代了完成故事的需要。

options.en: The group valued the public reading but found no pleasure in having written together.
options.zh: 小組重視公開朗讀，卻不覺合寫有任何樂趣。

listening.explanationZh: 合寫並完成已有樂趣，朗讀是額外好處；不是未完成或只為獲朗讀才開始。
listening.en: Finishing our first shared story was already a pleasure; having it read aloud at the village evening was the icing on the cake, not the reason we had begun writing together.
listening.zh: 完成第一篇合寫故事已令人高興；它在村裏晚會獲朗讀，更是錦上添花，並非我們開始合寫的原因。

reply.promptEn: Why do you call the village reading an extra pleasure?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼把村裏朗讀稱作額外喜悅？

options.en: We had already enjoyed completing the story together.
options.zh: 我們原已享受一起完成故事。

options.en: It was the icing on the cake because the writing had already been worthwhile to us.
options.zh: 寫作本來已值得，所以朗讀是錦上添花。

options.en: Being heard by others added to something we already valued.
options.zh: 別人聽到故事，在原有重視的事上再添好處。

options.en: We did not need the invitation to make our shared writing feel rewarding.
options.zh: 不用那份邀請，合寫也已讓我們感到有收穫。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均解釋已有主要喜悅，因而朗讀只是再添好處。

scene.promptZh: 虛構旅客本來很滿意展覽及導賞，離開時又獲贈一張喜歡的插畫卡。她想分清原有體驗與額外禮物。哪句貼切？

options.en: The illustration card was the icing on the cake after an exhibition I had already enjoyed.
options.zh: 展覽本來已讓我享受，插畫卡更是錦上添花。

options.en: The card was the only worthwhile part of a visit I otherwise disliked.
options.zh: 我原本不喜歡探訪，卡片是唯一值得的部分。

options.en: Receiving the card was the condition on which I had agreed to attend.
options.zh: 我先以收到卡片為條件，才答應到場。

scene.explanationZh: 本來滿意展覽及導賞，才有額外好處；不是唯一可取處或事先條件。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 the icing on the cake 的比喻？

options.en: A welcome extra improves an already satisfying experience.
options.zh: 受歡迎的額外好處，令本來滿意的經驗更好。

options.en: The supposed extra is the only thing that gives an otherwise unwanted experience any value.
options.zh: 所謂額外好處，是讓其餘全不想要的經驗有價值的唯一事物。

options.en: The main achievement still matters without the extra benefit.
options.zh: 沒有額外好處，主要成果仍然重要。

contrast.explanationZh: 錦上添花先有值得的基礎，不是用唯一好處抵銷其餘全部不滿。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友把小組介紹寫成「只為晚會朗讀才合寫」，但你們本來已享受寫作。你想怎澄清？

options.en: The reading was the icing on the cake; we had already found the writing rewarding before the invitation arrived.
options.zh: 朗讀是錦上添花；邀請到來前，我們已覺寫作有收穫。

options.en: An invitation should be our condition for the next story; without one, writing together would not be worthwhile.
options.zh: 下個故事應先有邀請才寫，沒有邀請，合寫便不值得。

options.en: I would judge the next shared story by whether it gets a public reading, rather than by what we enjoy making together.
options.zh: 我會按下篇合寫故事是否獲公開朗讀來判價值，不看我們一起創作的樂趣。

dialogue.explanationZh: 本來合寫已帶來樂趣，邀請是額外收穫；不能把邀請變成繼續創作的必要條件或唯一價值尺度。

speaking.en: The unexpected invitation was the icing on the cake, because we had already enjoyed making something together.
speaking.zh: 意外邀請是錦上添花，因我們本來已享受一起創作。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分主要收穫與額外喜悅。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你完成一個練習計劃，終能自己讀懂祖母的一封信，但未獲課程證書。朋友說沒證書就白費，你想說明真正想做到的事已做到，證書若有只是額外肯定。用一至兩句英文直接回覆，不假裝已獲證書。

examples.en: Reading my grandmother’s letter for myself was what I wanted to achieve. A certificate would have been the icing on the cake, not the only thing that made the work worthwhile.
examples.zh: 自己讀懂祖母的信，才是我想做到的事；若有證書會是錦上添花，不是令努力值得的唯一事物。

examples.en: I can now understand the letter without someone reading it to me, so the practice has mattered. The certificate would be the icing on the cake, but its absence does not take that achievement away.
examples.zh: 我現在不用別人代讀，也能明白那封信，所以練習有意義；證書會是錦上添花，但沒有它不會抹去這項成果。

glossary.en: without someone reading it to me

writing.selfCheckZh: 清楚保留讀懂家書的主要成果，用假設語氣說未得到的額外肯定；不把沒有證書改成練習全無價值。

takeaways.en: The friendly message was the icing on the cake after she had already enjoyed the afternoon’s music.
takeaways.zh: 她原已享受下午音樂，友善訊息更是錦上添花。

takeaways.en: Finishing the garden mattered most; the invitation to show it to visitors was the icing on the cake.
takeaways.zh: 完成花園最重要；獲邀向訪客展示，更是錦上添花。

sources.sentence: The players agreed to put in more effort.

brief.meaningEn: Devote a greater amount of attention, energy or work to a goal.
brief.meaningZh: 為某個目標投入更多專注、心力或工作。
brief.grammar: put/puts/putting in more effort; past put in. Put in here means devote; explain what the extra effort involves rather than measure it only by hours.
brief.register: Natural effort collocation with phrasal put in, rather than an opaque idiom. More effort does not itself establish a better method or successful result.
brief.boundaryZh: 多努力不等於只延長時間，也不保證成功；可具體說增加哪種準備、練習或查核。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不可用籠統「更努力」代替可做步驟，也不因結果未好便斷言沒有努力。
brief.outcomeZh: 能提出有目標的額外投入，分清投入與已證成果。

options.en: They planned focused comparison work involving claims, evidence and uncertainties.
options.zh: 他們計劃針對主張、證據及疑問作比較。

options.en: They decided that reading the pages again was the only preparation needed.
options.zh: 他們決定只需再讀一遍，便算準備完成。

options.en: They had already settled every uncertainty before agreeing on the new preparation.
options.zh: 議定新準備前，他們已解決每項疑問。

options.en: Each reader would prepare a separate summary without comparing any supporting details.
options.zh: 每人只備獨立摘要，不比較任何支持細節。

listening.explanationZh: 投入以明確步驟表現，屬計劃，未說疑問已全解或只重讀、摘要。
listening.en: We agreed to put in more effort when comparing the two accounts: each of us would mark the claim, find its supporting detail and bring one uncertainty to the discussion, rather than simply read the pages again.
listening.zh: 比較兩份敘述時，我們答應投入更多努力：各自標主張、找支持細節，並帶一項疑問來討論，不只是再讀一遍。

reply.promptEn: Why do you want to change how you prepare for the comparison?
reply.promptZh: 你們為甚麼想改比較前的準備方法？

options.en: We need to identify claims and evidence instead of only reading again.
options.zh: 我們需辨認主張與證據，不只再讀一遍。

options.en: Putting in more effort should mean examining what supports each account, not merely spending longer with the pages.
options.zh: 投入更多努力，應是查每份敘述有何支持，不只是看得更久。

options.en: Bringing an uncertainty would give the discussion a specific question to work on.
options.zh: 帶來一項疑問，可給討論一個具體問題。

options.en: The new steps would help us prepare material we can actually compare.
options.zh: 新步驟可幫我們準備真正能比較的資料。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均給改準備的具體用途，不把時間長短當唯一努力指標。

scene.promptZh: 角色多花一小時重畫海報邊框，卻沒有核展覽時間；她確實付出心力，但仍未處理同伴指出的資料錯誤。哪句準確？

options.en: She put in more effort on the border, but that did not address the unchecked exhibition time.
options.zh: 她在邊框投入更多努力，但未處理未核實的展覽時間。

options.en: She should spend the next hour adding decoration before checking the reported time error.
options.zh: 她應先再花一小時加裝飾，才核對已有人指出的時間錯誤。

options.en: Her extra work has mainly improved the information visitors need to choose when to arrive.
options.zh: 她新增的工作主要改善了訪客選何時到場所需的資料。

scene.explanationZh: 她確實在邊框投入心力，但到場時間仍未核；不能把裝飾當資料改善，也不應再延後已指出的資料問題。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 put in more effort 推出？

options.en: Someone increases the work or attention devoted to a task.
options.zh: 某人增加投入任務的工作或專注。

options.en: The extra effort proves that the chosen method has already produced the intended result.
options.zh: 額外努力，證明所選方法已帶來預期結果。

options.en: The context can identify what additional work the person does.
options.zh: 情境可指出當事人額外做了甚麼。

contrast.explanationZh: 投入與結果需分開，還要看方法及實際回饋。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴把「多努力」說成必須再讀三遍，卻不願找支持細節；你們任務是比較敘述。哪句最好？

options.en: Let us put in more effort by checking the claims against details; extra rereading alone may leave the comparison unchanged.
options.zh: 讓我們多查主張與細節，投入更多努力；只是再讀，未必改變比較。

options.en: Reading the pages three more times should be enough preparation; we can check the supporting details after submitting.
options.zh: 再讀三遍應已夠準備；提交後才查支持主張的細節吧。

options.en: If evidence checking takes time, we should drop the comparison and report only which page we prefer.
options.zh: 若核證據需時，就放棄比較，只報較喜歡哪頁。

dialogue.explanationZh: 比較需檢查主張與細節；重讀可有用途，但不能以次數代比較，也不宜交後才核必要證據或只報偏好。

speaking.en: I will put in more effort by practising the part I find difficult and asking for feedback on that part.
speaking.zh: 我會針對覺得難的部分練習，並求那部分的回饋，投入更多努力。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再用實際行動說明額外投入。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替一個故事人物寫道歉訊息。他答應幫朋友排練，卻總遲到，現在不想只說「我會更努力」。他要先查可用交通、提早出發，若不能準時就預先通知；尚未證明改好。用一至兩句第一人稱英文提出可檢視的承諾。

examples.en: I need to put in more effort to keep the rehearsal time I agreed to, not just apologise afterwards. I will check the journey, leave earlier and tell you in advance if I cannot arrive on time.
examples.zh: 我需投入更多努力，守住答應的排練時間，不只是事後道歉；我會查路程、提早出發，若不能準時便預先告訴你。

examples.en: Putting in more effort means changing how I plan the journey, so I will check the route before the next rehearsal. Please do not take this promise as proof that the problem is solved; I need to follow it through.
examples.zh: 投入更多努力，對我就是改路程規劃，所以下次排練前我會先查路線；請別把承諾當問題已解，我需實際做到。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把努力化為事前路程規劃及通知，不只重複道歉，也不把承諾說成已證明準時。

takeaways.en: She put in more effort on the unclear section, asking a reader which link was still missing.
takeaways.zh: 她在不清楚的部分投入更多努力，問讀者還缺哪項連結。

takeaways.en: Putting in more effort helped him notice the repeated error, although he still needed to test the correction.
takeaways.zh: 投入更多努力，幫他留意到重複錯誤，但更正仍需測試。

lessons.titleEn: light a fire under a child

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A well-chosen challenge can light a fire under a child.
sources.expression: light a fire under a child

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: If employees are delaying the task, a deadline may light a fire under them.

brief.meaningEn: Strongly motivate or prompt someone to act, often after delay or a lack of urgency.
brief.meaningZh: 強烈推動或促使某人行動，常用於原本拖延或欠迫切感的情況。
brief.grammar: light/lit/lighting a fire under someone; a deadline, challenge or clear request may be the prompt. The phrase describes a strong spur, not literal fire or a guarantee of good work.
brief.register: Informal motivation idiom. It can sound forceful; whether the prompt is supportive or harmful depends on the action and context.
brief.boundaryZh: 強烈推動不等於威嚇才有效，也不保證合乎負荷；要說實際提示及行動，不以比喻合理化傷害。
brief.misconceptionZh: 開始動工與做得好是兩件事；若困難是欠工具或時間，催促不能自行補足。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分清強烈促動、實際資源及其後品質，保留自主與可行安排。

listening.promptZh: 甚麼被促動，甚麼仍未備好？

options.en: The invitation prompted planning and role choices, while props still needed arranging.
options.zh: 邀請促成練習安排及分角，道具仍待安排。

options.en: The group had finished rehearsing the full piece before receiving the invitation.
options.zh: 收到邀請前，小組已排練完整段戲。

options.en: They used the booked practice to complete a full read-through with the props already in place.
options.zh: 他們在已訂練習中，道具齊備地完成了整段讀演。

options.en: The group declined to plan any practice and left the roles unassigned.
options.zh: 小組拒絕安排練習，也未分配角色。

listening.explanationZh: 已訂時間及分角色，顯示開始規劃；未報整段已排好，道具也仍待安排。
listening.en: An invitation to show a short scene lit a fire under the group: they stopped hesitating, booked a practice and chose roles, though they still needed props before rehearsing the full piece.
listening.zh: 獲邀展示一小段戲，強烈促使小組行動：他們不再猶豫，訂練習時間及分角色，但練整段前仍需道具。

reply.promptEn: Why do you say the invitation motivated the group?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼說邀請促使小組行動？

options.en: They booked a practice after hesitating about getting started.
options.zh: 他們原本猶豫要否開始，後來訂了練習時間。

options.en: It lit a fire under them, leading them to choose roles and arrange a practice.
options.zh: 它強烈促動他們，讓他們分角色及安排練習。

options.en: The chance to show a small scene gave them a concrete reason to begin.
options.zh: 展示一小段戲的機會，給他們開始的具體理由。

options.en: Their response changed from hesitation to practical planning.
options.zh: 他們由猶豫，轉為實際規劃。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均以已見的開始行動說促動，不把邀請當所有條件或品質已具備。

scene.promptZh: 學員願做模型，但一直缺所需材料；導師只加一個近限期，未提供材料，仍不能動工。哪句最準確？

options.en: A deadline might light a fire under someone who is delaying, but it does not supply this learner’s missing materials.
options.zh: 限期或可強烈促使拖延的人行動，但不會供給這學員缺少的材料。

options.en: The learner’s main difficulty is choosing which model to make before the deadline.
options.zh: 學員的主要困難，是在限期前決定做哪個模型。

options.en: The learner has the materials but needs a firmer reminder to begin.
options.zh: 學員已有材料，只需更強提醒才開始。

scene.explanationZh: 學員願做，已知阻礙是缺材料；不是尚未選模型，也不能只把問題判作欠提醒。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 light a fire under someone 的比喻推出？

options.en: A prompt strongly encourages or pressures someone to act.
options.zh: 某項提示強烈鼓勵或催促某人行動。

options.en: A stronger prompt necessarily removes the practical obstacle that was preventing the work.
options.zh: 更強催促，必定移除原本阻止工作的實際障礙。

options.en: The context should show what changed in the person’s actions.
options.zh: 情境應顯示當事人行動有何改變。

contrast.explanationZh: 促動與供應工具、時間或支援不同，實際障礙需另外處理。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴見小組開始規劃，便說不必再安排道具，邀請已令他們「動起來」；整段排練仍需道具。哪句最好？

options.en: The invitation lit a fire under them, but we still need to arrange the props so their planning can become a full rehearsal.
options.zh: 邀請促動他們，但仍需安排道具，才能把規劃變成整段排練。

options.en: Bring the full rehearsal forward and let the group discover the missing props when they arrive.
options.zh: 把整段排練提早，讓小組到場才發現缺道具。

options.en: The props should be requested only after the first full rehearsal shows which ones were missing.
options.zh: 應留待首次整段排練顯示缺甚麼道具後，才提出要求。

dialogue.explanationZh: 開始規劃值得肯定，仍需實際條件；不能把已知道具需要留到現場，或等整段排練後才要求。

speaking.en: The challenge lit a fire under the group, but we still checked that they had the time and materials to take the next step.
speaking.zh: 挑戰促使小組行動，但我們仍查他們是否有時間及材料做下一步。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分促動與實際支持。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你自己選本周五為整理家庭舊地圖的限期，這令你終於開始按年份分類；朋友以為家人逼你。你想澄清限期是自己定，也請他借出幾張仍缺的舊照片。用一至兩句英文直接回覆。

examples.en: I chose Friday myself, and that deadline lit a fire under me to start sorting the family maps by year. Nobody forced me; could you lend me the old photographs so I can check the places I have not identified?
examples.zh: 星期五是我自己選的，那限期促使我開始按年分類家裏舊地圖；沒人逼我，可借舊照片給我核仍未認出的地方嗎？

examples.en: It was my own deadline that lit a fire under me, not pressure from my family. I have begun arranging the maps, but I still need the old photographs to work out which places they show.
examples.zh: 促使我行動的是自己定的限期，不是家人施壓；我已開始排地圖，但仍需舊照片來辨認它們畫哪些地方。

glossary.en: sorting the family maps by year
glossary.zh: 按年份分類家裏舊地圖

glossary.en: the places I have not identified

writing.selfCheckZh: 說清自己定限期及已開始分類，回應朋友對強迫的誤會，再提出借照片的具體需要；不把有動力當資源已齊。

takeaways.en: The approaching exhibition lit a fire under the team, and they finally agreed on which pieces to practise first.
takeaways.zh: 展期將近，促使小組行動，他們終於議定先練哪些作品。

takeaways.en: The chance to interview the retired driver lit a fire under me, and I finally sorted my notes into questions for him.
takeaways.zh: 有機會訪問退休司機，強烈促使我行動，我終於把筆記整理成問他的問題。

No claim literal force is justified.

sources.sentence: Learners can work at their own pace.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Learners can work at their own pace.

brief.meaningEn: At a speed suited to the person, with room to spend more or less time as needed.
brief.meaningZh: 按適合自己的速度進行，可按需要多花或少花時間。
brief.grammar: work/learn/read at one’s own pace; the possessive identifies whose speed is being accommodated. It does not itself remove an agreed deadline or the need to coordinate shared work.
brief.register: Conventional pace phrase. Different speeds need not indicate different worth or commitment.
brief.boundaryZh: 自己的步調不等於完全沒有期限或任意延誤他人的安排；個人練習與共同交接要分清。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可給暫停、重聽或較快略過熟悉部分的選擇，不預設人人同速才公平。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明個人可調節甚麼，以及共同安排仍需怎協調。

listening.promptZh: 個人步調與共同安排怎並存？

options.en: They controlled how long to spend on different parts, while keeping a shared practice plan.
options.zh: 他們自行調節各部分所需時間，同時保留共同練習計劃。

options.en: Both were required to pause and restart at exactly the same points.
options.zh: 兩人被要求在完全相同位置暫停及重看。

options.en: The recording replaced the Saturday practice, which they had already cancelled.
options.zh: 錄製示範取代星期六練習，兩人已取消聚會。

options.en: Mira replayed only the part she already knew and skipped the unfamiliar turn.
options.zh: Mira 只重看熟悉部分，略過陌生轉身。

listening.explanationZh: 可按熟悉程度調速度，仍保星期六練習；不是同點暫停或已取消聚會。
listening.en: The recorded demonstration let Mira learn at her own pace: she paused at the unfamiliar turn and replayed it, while her partner moved through a part he already knew; both still planned to meet for practice on Saturday.
listening.zh: 錄製示範讓 Mira 按自己的步調學；她在陌生轉身處暫停重看，伙伴則較快看過已熟悉部分；兩人仍打算星期六一起練。

reply.promptEn: Why was the recording useful for Mira’s preparation?
reply.promptZh: 錄製示範為甚麼有助 Mira 準備？

options.en: She could pause and replay the unfamiliar turn.
options.zh: 她可在陌生轉身處暫停重看。

options.en: It let her learn at her own pace rather than follow her partner through every part.
options.zh: 它讓她按自己的步調學，不用每部分都跟伙伴同速。

options.en: She could spend more time where she needed it before the shared practice.
options.zh: 一起練之前，她可在有需要的地方多花時間。

options.en: Her partner’s familiarity did not require her to skip the part she still needed to see.
options.zh: 伙伴已熟悉，不表示她也需略過仍想看的部分。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均答可調節陌生部分的準備，不把不同速度當能力或態度的評價。

scene.promptZh: 現場課程規定每人同一分鐘開始、同一分鐘轉下一題，不可暫停或回看；這描述只關乎該節活動。哪句最準確？

options.en: This particular activity does not let each learner work at their own pace.
options.zh: 這一節活動，並不讓每位學員按自己的步調做。

options.en: The shared timing means every learner has chosen how long to spend on each question.
options.zh: 統一時間，表示每位學員已自選每題做多久。

options.en: The schedule confirms that all learners need the same amount of time to understand each question.
options.zh: 時間表確認所有學員理解每題所需時間相同。

scene.explanationZh: 統一且不能暫停的流程，未提供個人調速；也未證每人的需要相同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜單憑 at their own pace 推出？

options.en: People can proceed at a speed that suits them.
options.zh: 大家可按適合自己的速度進行。

options.en: They are automatically released from every previously agreed shared deadline.
options.zh: 他們自動免除所有先前議定的共同期限。

options.en: The context should show which timing choices they can make.
options.zh: 情境應顯示他們可調節哪些時間安排。

contrast.explanationZh: 個人調速與共同承諾不同，期限若需改應另協商。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說 Mira 重看轉身是拖小組進度，要她跟伙伴同速；兩人仍照原定星期六練。哪句最好？

options.en: She can prepare at her own pace and still meet on Saturday; replaying the unfamiliar part is part of getting ready.
options.zh: 她可按自己的步調準備，也照常星期六聚會；重看陌生部分，是準備的一環。

options.en: She should skip the turn because her partner has already understood it.
options.zh: 伙伴已明白，所以她應略過那個轉身。

options.en: We should cancel Saturday now rather than ask how her preparation is going.
options.zh: 不用問她準備得怎樣，現在便應取消星期六聚會。

dialogue.explanationZh: 保留已定安排及個人所需準備，不用伙伴速度代她需要，也不預先取消。

speaking.en: I can work at my own pace on this part, while agreeing a clear handover time with the people who need it next.
speaking.zh: 這部分我可按自己的步調做，同時跟之後需用的人議定清楚交接時間。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把個人速度與共同交接分開。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你和伙伴合寫小冊，各自負責不同章。你想慢慢查自己那章的訪談，但伙伴需在排版前拿到稿。用一至兩句英文直接向伙伴提出：你會按自己步調查資料，同時一起訂一個實際交稿日；若未能趕及會預先談範圍，不讓對方一直等。

examples.en: I would like to check the interviews at my own pace, but I know you need the chapter before layout. Could we agree a realistic handover date and discuss a smaller scope in advance if I cannot meet it?
examples.zh: 我想按自己的步調核訪談，但知道你排版前需收到章稿；可否議一個實際交稿日，若我未能趕及，便預先談縮小範圍？

examples.en: Working at my own pace should not leave you waiting without a plan. Let us set a chapter deadline together, and I will tell you early if the checking needs a change of scope.
examples.zh: 按自己步調工作，不應讓你毫無計劃地等；一起定章稿期限吧，若查核需調範圍，我會提早告訴你。

writing.selfCheckZh: 同時說個人查核需要及伙伴的後續工作，提出實際日期與事前商量，不把自主步調當無限延後承諾。

takeaways.en: The quiet reading session let her follow the argument at her own pace instead of rushing to match the next reader.
takeaways.zh: 安靜閱讀時段讓她按自己的步調理解論點，不用趕上下一位讀者。

takeaways.en: They prepared at their own pace during the week, then brought their questions to the agreed group meeting.
takeaways.zh: 他們在周內按自己的步調準備，再把問題帶到議定的小組聚會。

lessons.titleEn: lifts children up rather than weighs them down
lessons.titleZh: 鼓舞孩子，而非加重負擔

target.pattern: \blift(?:s|ed|ing)? (?:children|the children|them|us|me|you|him|her) up rather than weigh(?:s|ed|ing)? (?:children|the children|them|us|me|you|him|her) down\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Good feedback lifts children up rather than weighs them down.
sources.expression: lifts children up rather than weighs them down

brief.meaningEn: Encourage children and help them feel able to act, rather than add discouragement or an emotional burden.
brief.meaningZh: 鼓勵孩子，讓他們覺得有能力採取行動，而非增加灰心或情緒負擔。
brief.grammar: feedback can lift children up rather than weigh them down; lifts/weighs in a finite present sentence. The paired vertical/weight images concern emotional effect, not physical lifting or measured body weight.
brief.register: Contextual contrast of familiar encouragement and burden metaphors. Supportive feedback may still identify a real error and a difficult next step.
brief.boundaryZh: 鼓舞不等於只讚不指出問題，也不表示一次回饋解決所有困難；要看措辭及可做步驟。
brief.misconceptionZh: 空泛「你最棒」未必提供方向，指出錯誤也不必變成人格否定。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把鼓勵連到具體可行修訂，分清作品問題與孩子整體價值。

listening.promptZh: 鼓勵與指出問題怎並存？

options.en: The feedback combined a specific strength and a possible revision without judging the children’s whole ability.
options.zh: 回饋結合具體優點及可試修訂，不評斷孩子的整體能力。

options.en: The teacher removed every suggestion for change and praised only the children’s talent.
options.zh: 老師刪掉所有修改建議，只讚孩子天分。

options.en: A confusing draft was treated as evidence that the children could not become writers.
options.zh: 首稿混亂，被當成孩子不可能成為作者的證據。

options.en: The teacher had rewritten the drafts for the children before asking them to try a change.
options.zh: 老師請孩子試改前，已替他們重寫稿件。

listening.explanationZh: 具體優點與可做改動可同時給支持，不是只讚、貼能力標籤或代做。
listening.en: The teacher wanted feedback to lift children up rather than weigh them down, so she named one clear strength and one change they could try, without calling a confusing first draft proof that they were bad writers.
listening.zh: 老師想回饋鼓舞孩子而非加重負擔，所以指出一項明確優點及一項可試的改動，不把首稿混亂說成他們是差勁作者的證明。

reply.promptEn: Why did the teacher give both a strength and a possible change?
reply.promptZh: 老師為甚麼同時給優點及可試改動？

options.en: The children could see something to keep and a specific next action.
options.zh: 孩子可看見應保留甚麼，以及下一個具體行動。

options.en: She wanted feedback to lift children up rather than weigh them down by making the revision feel possible.
options.zh: 她想讓修訂顯得可做，使回饋鼓舞孩子而非加重負擔。

options.en: Naming a strength helped her discuss a problem without defining the children by that problem.
options.zh: 指出優點，讓她可談問題，而不以問題定義孩子。

options.en: The comment gave a direction for another draft instead of ending with a judgement of their worth.
options.zh: 評語給下一稿方向，不以個人價值判斷作結。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均說明具體且不貼標籤的回饋，怎讓下一步可見。

scene.promptZh: 導師只說「你們最有天分」，沒有指作品哪裏有效或要怎改；孩子仍不知道下一步。你想謹慎評估這項稱讚。哪句最準確？

options.en: The praise is positive, but the account does not yet show that it helps the children choose a next revision.
options.zh: 稱讚是正面的，但敘述尚未顯示它能幫孩子選下一項修訂。

options.en: The positive words confirm that the children now know which paragraph to revise.
options.zh: 正面字句，確認孩子現已知道要改哪段。

options.en: The children have been given a worked example of how to connect the paragraphs.
options.zh: 孩子已獲一個示範，說明怎連接段落。

scene.explanationZh: 正面語氣未自動給具體方向，資料沒提段落修法或示範。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 lift children up rather than weigh them down 的回饋方向？

options.en: Identify a useful feature and a manageable change without labelling the child.
options.zh: 指出有用特點及可應付的改動，不替孩子貼標籤。

options.en: Treat one mistaken answer as a verdict on the child’s worth.
options.zh: 把一次答錯，當作孩子個人價值的定論。

options.en: Keep a challenging learning goal while explaining what the child can try next.
options.zh: 保留有挑戰的學習目標，同時解釋孩子下一步可試甚麼。

contrast.explanationZh: 可談錯誤及挑戰，但不把一項表現升格為人的價值定論。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說怕孩子灰心就不能指出稿件問題；你想保留真正需要的修訂。哪句最好？

options.en: Feedback can lift children up rather than weigh them down while naming a real problem; let us make the next change clear and avoid labels about talent.
options.zh: 指出真問題時，回饋仍可鼓舞孩子而非加重負擔；讓下一項改動清楚，避免貼天分標籤吧。

options.en: We should leave the confusing passage unmentioned and tell them the draft needs no changes.
options.zh: 應略過混亂段落，告訴他們稿件不需修改。

options.en: Ask for a complete rewrite without saying which part is confusing, so the comment stays brief.
options.zh: 為讓評語簡短，要求整篇重寫，但不說哪部分混亂。

dialogue.explanationZh: 支持可包含清楚問題及方向；不是隱瞞需要，也不是只加大工作而不給線索。

speaking.en: I want this feedback to lift children up rather than weigh them down, with an honest description of the problem and one possible next step.
speaking.zh: 我想這回饋鼓舞孩子而非加重負擔，誠實說明問題，再給一個可行下一步。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把鼓勵與具體修訂並看。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替故事中的孩子寫給成人的短訊。她收到幾份互相矛盾的修改意見，不是不願改，而是不知先聽哪項。她想請成人一起揀一項先試，並問清楚它想改善甚麼，不要求取消回饋。用一至兩句英文，以孩子身份提出具體請求。

examples.en: I want feedback to lift me up rather than weigh me down, but these different instructions leave me unsure where to start. Could we choose one change together and explain what it is meant to improve?
examples.zh: 我希望回饋鼓勵我而非加重我的負擔，但這些不同指示令我不知從哪開始；可否一起選一項改動，說明想改善甚麼？

examples.en: Could we make these comments lift me up rather than weigh me down by agreeing which suggestion I should try first? I am willing to revise, but I need to understand the purpose before trying to follow conflicting advice.
examples.zh: 可否先議我應試哪項建議，讓這些評語鼓勵我而非加重我的負擔？我願修訂，但照互相矛盾的意見做之前，需先明白目的。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以孩子身份指出多重指示的困難，請成人共訂一項優先及目的，不把求清楚當拒絕改，也不要求刪去所有回饋。

takeaways.en: The coach wanted the discussion to lift children up rather than weigh them down, so she separated the missed pass from a judgement about the player.
takeaways.zh: 教練想討論鼓舞孩子而非加重負擔，所以把漏接球與對球員的整體評價分開。

takeaways.en: The comments can lift children up rather than weigh them down when they make a difficult next step understandable.
takeaways.zh: 評語讓困難的下一步變得可理解時，便可鼓舞孩子而非加重負擔。

sources.sentence: A pat on the back helped, but she also needed resources.

brief.meaningEn: Praise or an expression of approval for something someone has done.
brief.meaningZh: 對某人所做事情的稱讚或肯定。
brief.grammar: give/get/deserve a pat on the back for + action; metaphorical praise need not involve a physical touch. State what is being praised.
brief.register: Informal approval idiom. A brief compliment can be sincere and useful without constituting a full assessment or providing practical support.
brief.boundaryZh: 獲肯定不等於整份作品已通過，也不表示之後不用支援或可替對方作承諾。
brief.misconceptionZh: 稱讚可以有價值，但需分清它針對的行動及仍未評估的部分。
brief.outcomeZh: 能理解肯定的具體範圍，並在需要時提出進一步回饋。

listening.promptZh: 稱讚的範圍及仍待做的事是甚麼？

options.en: The new ending received praise, while the rest of the manuscript still awaited discussion.
options.zh: 新結尾獲稱讚，其餘稿件仍待討論。

options.en: The editor approved the entire manuscript and cancelled the next meeting.
options.zh: 編輯通過整份稿件，並取消下次會議。

options.en: The message criticised the added link and asked Mira to remove it before meeting.
options.zh: 訊息批評新增連結，叫 Mira 開會前刪去。

options.en: Mira had already discussed the whole manuscript before receiving the comment on the ending.
options.zh: 收到結尾評語前，Mira 已討論過整份稿件。

listening.explanationZh: 肯定針對結尾新增連結，其餘仍待下周討論；不是整稿通過或要求刪掉。
listening.en: The editor’s message was a pat on the back for Mira’s clearer ending: it praised the link she had added, but said the rest of the manuscript would be discussed at next week’s meeting.
listening.zh: 編輯訊息是對 Mira 較清楚結尾的肯定：它稱讚新增連結，但說其餘稿件要到下周會議才討論。

reply.promptEn: Why did Mira feel encouraged by the editor’s message?
reply.promptZh: Mira 為甚麼受編輯訊息鼓勵？

options.en: The editor noticed and praised the link she had added to the ending.
options.zh: 編輯留意並稱讚她在結尾加的連結。

options.en: It was a pat on the back for a specific improvement she had made.
options.zh: 它肯定了她作出的一項具體改善。

options.en: Her work on making the ending clearer had been recognised.
options.zh: 她讓結尾更清楚的努力，獲得認同。

options.en: The comment showed that the new link was working for that reader.
options.zh: 評語顯示新增連結對那位讀者有效。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均說明獲認同的具體改動，未把局部肯定擴成整稿結論。

scene.promptZh: 教練說「這次接棒慢，下一次留意訊號」，沒有稱讚或表達認同；你要分清評語功能，不判它是否有用。哪句準確？

options.en: This is a correction with a next step, rather than a pat on the back.
options.zh: 這是帶下一步的糾正，不是稱讚或肯定。

options.en: The comment praises how well the baton change went this time.
options.zh: 評語是在稱讚這次接棒做得好。

options.en: The coach has approved the whole race plan without asking for a change.
options.zh: 教練已通過整個賽跑計劃，沒有要求改動。

scene.explanationZh: 有用糾正不必是稱讚；不能因提出下一步就當已肯定現有表現。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只憑 someone received a pat on the back 推出？

options.en: Someone expressed approval of an action or achievement.
options.zh: 有人對一項行動或成果表達認同。

options.en: A complete assessment has approved every part of the person’s work.
options.zh: 完整評估已通過當事人工作的每個部分。

options.en: The context can identify what the praise refers to.
options.zh: 情境可指出稱讚針對甚麼。

contrast.explanationZh: 肯定與全面審核不同，要看所指範圍。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友把編輯訊息當整稿已可出版，想跳過下周討論；訊息只讚結尾。哪句最好？

options.en: It is a pat on the back for the ending, not approval of the whole manuscript; keep the meeting for the parts still to discuss.
options.zh: 它是對結尾的肯定，不是整稿通過；保留會議，談仍待討論的部分吧。

options.en: I would send the manuscript straight to the printer now, since praise for the ending is enough for the next stage.
options.zh: 我會現在直接把整稿交印刷，因為讚結尾已足以進下一階段。

options.en: The editor probably meant only that we should stop revising the ending and use the meeting for a new project.
options.zh: 編輯可能只想我們停改結尾，把會議改作談新項目。

dialogue.explanationZh: 訊息肯定結尾，但其餘章節仍有待談；保留原會議，不自行把局部稱讚當交印依據，也不改成另一項目。

speaking.en: I appreciated the pat on the back, and I still wanted to know which part of the work needed attention next.
speaking.zh: 我感謝那份肯定，也仍想知道工作哪部分下一步需留意。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分認同與進一步回饋。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你第一次帶小組討論，伙伴只說「做得好」。你感到獲鼓勵，但想學會怎讓較安靜的人加入；你不要求伙伴再多讚，而想請他指出一個你可保留的提問，以及下一次可試的邀請方法。用一至兩句英文回覆。

examples.en: Thank you for the pat on the back; it helped me feel less nervous about leading. Could you point to one question that worked and suggest how I might invite a quieter person into the next discussion?
examples.zh: 謝謝你的肯定，讓我帶領時沒那麼緊張；可否指出一個有效問題，再建議下次怎邀較安靜的人加入討論？

examples.en: I appreciate a pat on the back, but I would also like specific feedback on participation. Which question should I keep, and what could I try when someone has not spoken yet?
examples.zh: 我感謝肯定，也想有關參與的具體回饋；哪個問題應保留？有人還未發言時，我可試甚麼？

writing.selfCheckZh: 接受鼓勵，同時請求有關邀請參與的具體觀察；不把一句稱讚當完整帶領指導，也不要求別人一定發言。

takeaways.en: The volunteers deserved a pat on the back for keeping the welcome calm when several guests arrived together.
takeaways.zh: 幾位嘉賓同時到場時，義工仍保持從容迎接，值得肯定。

takeaways.en: Her message gave him a pat on the back for the revised question without claiming that the whole interview was ready.
takeaways.zh: 她的訊息肯定他改過的問題，沒有聲稱整份訪問已準備好。

lessons.titleZh: 投入資源培育及支持人才

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Strong employers invest in people through mentoring.

brief.meaningEn: Devote resources to people’s development, abilities or well-being.
brief.meaningZh: 把資源投入人的發展、能力或福祉。
brief.grammar: invest time/money/support in people; investing in people can include mentoring, equipment, learning time or other support. This does not mean buying ownership of people.
brief.register: Conventional investment metaphor for human development. It highlights resources and longer-term support without guaranteeing a particular financial return.
brief.boundaryZh: 培育支持可有多種形式，不保證立即增產或獲利，也不等於對人有所有權。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要看實際資源及受助者需要，不只把口號、預算或獎金本身當已完成培訓。
brief.outcomeZh: 能具體描述投入與人的需要，分清承諾、已提供支援及後續成效。

listening.promptZh: 已提供甚麼，甚麼仍未評估？

options.en: Time and mentoring support had begun, while independent skill use was still to be evaluated.
options.zh: 時間及師友支援已開始，獨立運用能力仍待評估。

options.en: The workshop had only written a slogan, with no learning sessions yet started.
options.zh: 工場只寫了口號，學習活動尚未開始。

options.en: The evaluation had already established that each newcomer could work independently.
options.zh: 評估已確立每位新人都能獨立工作。

options.en: Newcomers were asked to learn entirely outside paid time without a partner.
options.zh: 新人被要求只在無薪時間自行學習，沒有伙伴。

listening.explanationZh: 有薪學習及結伴已提供，但成效仍待評估；不只是口號，也不是已證獨立。
listening.en: The workshop decided to invest in people by reserving paid learning time and pairing newcomers with experienced makers; the first sessions had begun, but the team had not yet evaluated what skills participants could use independently.
listening.zh: 工場決定投入資源支持人才，留出有薪學習時間，並讓新人跟有經驗製作者合作；首批活動已開始，但尚未評估參加者可獨立運用哪些能力。

reply.promptEn: Why does the workshop describe this as supporting people’s development?
reply.promptZh: 工場為甚麼說這是在支持人的發展？

options.en: Newcomers have learning time and access to experienced makers.
options.zh: 新人有學習時間，也有經驗製作者可請教。

options.en: It is investing in people through practical time and mentoring, not only announcing an aim.
options.zh: 它透過實際時間及師友支援投入人才，不只是宣布目標。

options.en: Participants can practise with support instead of being expected to arrive with every skill.
options.zh: 參加者可在支援下練習，不需一到便具備所有能力。

options.en: The arrangement commits resources to learning before judging independent performance.
options.zh: 安排先把資源投在學習，再評估獨立表現。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均以可用支援說投入，不把人當財產或把投入直接當利潤。

scene.promptZh: 學會已批出明年導師預算，尚未邀導師或辦活動；你想準確寫進度。哪句合適？

options.en: The club plans to invest in people through mentoring, but the sessions have not yet been arranged.
options.zh: 學會計劃透過師友支援投入人才，但活動尚未安排。

options.en: Approving the budget confirms that members have completed the mentoring programme.
options.zh: 批預算確認成員已完成師友計劃。

options.en: The club has already checked which mentoring skills each member can use alone.
options.zh: 學會已核過每位成員可獨立運用哪些師友技巧。

scene.explanationZh: 預算是承諾或準備，未等於已辦、完成或評估。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 invest in people 推出？

options.en: Resources are devoted to people’s development or support.
options.zh: 資源被投入人的發展或支援。

options.en: The support has necessarily produced an immediate financial return.
options.zh: 支援必定已帶來即時金錢回報。

options.en: The context should identify who receives which resources.
options.zh: 情境應指出誰得到哪種資源。

contrast.explanationZh: 投入與回報不同，也需看人的需要及實際使用。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴見活動開始便想宣傳「新人已能完全獨立」；評估還未做。哪句最好？

options.en: We are investing in people by providing time and mentoring; let us describe that support and wait for evidence about independent skills.
options.zh: 我們正提供時間及師友支援來培育人才；先描述支援，獨立能力則等證據吧。

options.en: Working with an experienced maker is already enough evidence that a newcomer can do the same task alone.
options.zh: 跟有經驗製作者合作，已足以證明新人能獨自做同一任務。

options.en: Delay the learning sessions until newcomers can demonstrate the skills without help.
options.zh: 等新人能毋須幫忙展示能力後，才開始學習活動。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可報已開始的投入，但有支援的合作不等於已證能獨自做；也不應等新人已會才提供學習。

speaking.en: Investing in people means making useful support available, then listening to how they can use it and what else they need.
speaking.zh: 投入資源支持人才，是讓有用支援可得，再聽他們怎運用及還需甚麼。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把資源、需要與使用連起來。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你獲一個創作資助計劃提供昂貴軟件，但你真正缺的是安靜使用設備的時間及字幕協助。你感謝資源，也想請主辦人先跟參加者核需要，不假定所有人缺同一工具。用一至兩句英文直接提出具體建議。

examples.en: If we want to invest in people, could we ask participants which support they can actually use before buying the same software for everyone? For me, quiet access time and help with captions would make a more practical difference.
examples.zh: 若想投入資源支持人才，給每人買同一軟件前，可否先問參加者實際能用甚麼支援？對我，安靜使用設備的時間及字幕協助更有實際作用。

examples.en: Thank you for investing in people through the grant, but my main barriers are time to use the equipment and caption support. Could we discuss those needs rather than assume that another tool is the answer for every participant?
examples.zh: 謝謝計劃投入資源支持人才，但我的主要困難是使用設備的時間及字幕支援；可否談這些需要，不假定添一件工具便是每位參加者的答案？

writing.selfCheckZh: 以參加者身份說具體可用支援，保留感謝並請先核需要，不否定所有工具，也不替其他人編相同困難。

takeaways.en: The organisation invested in people by giving experienced volunteers time to support the next group of newcomers.
takeaways.zh: 機構留出時間，讓有經驗義工支援下一批新人，投入資源培育人才。

takeaways.en: They are investing in people, but they still ask participants whether the learning arrangements fit their circumstances.
takeaways.zh: 他們正投入資源支持人才，但仍問參加者學習安排是否配合實際處境。

sources.sentence: Managers should not hand out rewards without clear criteria.

brief.meaningEn: Distribute rewards or prizes to recipients.
brief.meaningZh: 把獎勵或獎品派給領取者。
brief.grammar: hand out rewards/prizes; hand the rewards out; with a pronoun, hand them out. Selecting recipients and distributing the rewards are different stages.
brief.register: Common distribution phrasal verb. Hand out can describe physical items or metaphorical benefits; this lesson uses actual rewards and does not imply they were deserved or undeserved without criteria.
brief.boundaryZh: 派發不自動代表準則公平，也不等於只列名單；需分選人、公布及實際交付。
brief.misconceptionZh: 準則、記錄及未核個案要另交代，不由派發動作推誰一定值得。
brief.outcomeZh: 能準確說獎勵派到哪個階段，並提出需澄清的依據。

listening.promptZh: 派發進度及留下一張的原因是甚麼？

options.en: Rewards were distributed using the stated checklist, with one certificate awaiting collection.
options.zh: 獎勵按已說明清單派發，一張證書仍待領取。

options.en: The leader had not distributed any rewards and had only drafted the checklist.
options.zh: 領隊還未派任何獎勵，只草擬了清單。

options.en: The remaining certificate showed that its recipient had failed the agreed tasks.
options.zh: 留下證書，顯示領取者未完成議定任務。

options.en: The certificate had been withdrawn because the leader changed the criteria during the session.
options.zh: 領隊在活動中改準則，所以撤回那張證書。

listening.explanationZh: 已派發，留一張只因稍後領取；不是未派、未達標或改準則撤回。
listening.en: At the closing session, the leader handed out rewards for the agreed rehearsal tasks and explained the checklist used; one certificate stayed on the table because its recipient had left early and would collect it later.
listening.zh: 結束活動時，領隊按議定排練任務派發獎勵，並解釋所用清單；一張證書仍留桌上，因領取者早走，會稍後取回。

reply.promptEn: Why was one certificate still on the table after the session?
reply.promptZh: 活動後，為甚麼桌上仍有一張證書？

options.en: Its recipient had left early and would collect it later.
options.zh: 領取者提早離開，稍後才取。

options.en: We handed out rewards at the session, but that person was no longer there to receive theirs.
options.zh: 我們在活動派發獎勵，但那人已不在場領取。

options.en: The intended recipient was no longer at the session to collect it, so it stayed for later collection.
options.zh: 原定領取者已不在活動現場，所以證書留下待稍後領取。

options.en: The person’s early departure affected collection, not the stated decision to award it.
options.zh: 提早離開影響領取，不是改變已說明的頒發決定。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均說實際缺席與待領狀態，不以桌上有證書推不合資格。

scene.promptZh: 評審已議定獎項名單，尚未公布或通知，也還未把獎品交任何人。哪句準確？

options.en: The recipients have been selected, but the team has not yet handed out the rewards.
options.zh: 領獎者已選定，但小組尚未派發獎勵。

options.en: Choosing the names means everyone has already received a prize.
options.zh: 選好名字，表示每人已收到獎品。

options.en: The absence of a public announcement means no selection has been made.
options.zh: 未公開宣布，表示還沒有選人。

scene.explanationZh: 選定、公布及交付是不同階段，不能只用其中一項代全部。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個說法最不符合 hand out rewards 的派發用法？

options.en: The organisers distribute the rewards to the recipients.
options.zh: 主辦者把獎勵派給領取者。

options.en: The committee privately chooses the recipients but keeps every reward undistributed.
options.zh: 委員會私下選定領取者，但所有獎勵都未交付。

options.en: The prizes are ready, and the host hands them out after explaining the process.
options.zh: 獎品已備好，主持解釋程序後把它們派出。

contrast.explanationZh: 只選人但未交付，不等於已派發。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友想因桌上留一張證書，就說那人未達任務要求；你知道她只是早走。哪句最好？

options.en: We handed out rewards, and hers is waiting for collection; do not treat an uncollected certificate as a decision against her.
options.zh: 我們已派發獎勵，她那張仍待領；別把未領證書當不頒給她的決定。

options.en: Remove her name from the recipients because the certificate remained after the session.
options.zh: 活動後證書仍在，所以應把她從領獎名單刪去。

options.en: The certificate is still there, so the decision to award it must not have been made yet.
options.zh: 證書仍在，表示頒發決定一定還未作出。

dialogue.explanationZh: 按已知頒發與領取分開；未領不表示不合資格，也不表示頒發決定尚未作出。

speaking.en: Before we hand out rewards, let us make the criteria and collection arrangements clear to the people involved.
speaking.zh: 派發獎勵前，讓我們向相關人士說清準則及領取安排。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分準則、選定及交付。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你協助學會派發參與獎，紙本出席與網上記錄不一致，尚未查清幾名成員是否達標。伙伴想今天就公開「未合資格」名單。你想先核差異、私下問本人，確認後再派，不用不完整記錄判人。用一至兩句英文提出實際安排。

examples.en: Before we hand out rewards or publish a list of people who did not qualify, let us compare the paper and online records. We should ask the members about the gaps privately instead of treating an incomplete entry as a final decision.
examples.zh: 派發獎勵或公布未合資格名單前，先比較紙本及網上記錄；應私下問成員資料缺口，不把不完整紀錄當最後決定。

examples.en: We can hand the rewards out once the attendance differences have been checked. For now, please contact the members privately and keep the uncertain cases out of any public judgement.
examples.zh: 出席資料差異查清後，便可派發獎勵；目前請私下聯絡成員，不對未確定個案作公開判斷。

writing.selfCheckZh: 先核不一致資料及私下詢問，分清待查與已判不合資格；不以未完整記錄公開貼標籤，也不假稱已派。

takeaways.en: They handed out prizes after explaining which contributions the awards recognised.
takeaways.zh: 他們先解釋獎項認同哪些貢獻，再派發獎品。

takeaways.en: The rewards were ready, but the organiser waited for the recipients before handing them out.
takeaways.zh: 獎勵已備好，但主辦者等領取者到場後才派出。

sources.sentence: The trainee will take charge of the new project.

brief.meaningEn: Assume responsibility for managing or organising something.
brief.meaningZh: 負起管理或統籌某事的責任。
brief.grammar: take/took/taken/taking charge of + activity/group/process; specify the scope. A person in charge can coordinate others without doing every task alone.
brief.register: Common responsibility phrase. Taking charge of an agreed part does not grant control over every related decision.
brief.boundaryZh: 負責不等於包辦所有工作，也不代表擁有無限權限；要說明範圍及需要的協作。
brief.misconceptionZh: 自告奮勇應配合共同安排，不能未問就接管別人仍保有的決定。
brief.outcomeZh: 能準確說承擔哪部分，交代協調與他人保留的選擇。

listening.promptZh: 他的責任與界限是甚麼？

options.en: He coordinated practical arrangements while referring membership policy to the committee.
options.zh: 他統籌實際安排，把會員政策問題交委員會。

options.en: He changed the membership rules without consulting the committee.
options.zh: 他未問委員會便改會員規則。

options.en: He left the table cover unassigned and waited for the committee to set every collection time.
options.zh: 他未分配桌位人手，等委員會定每個收書時間。

options.en: He ran the tables himself without asking other helpers to cover them.
options.zh: 他自行照顧各桌，沒有請其他幫手當值。

listening.explanationZh: 他有協調分工，並轉交政策問題；不是自行改規則、未安排人手或親自包辦各桌。
listening.en: Ravi took charge of the book exchange by agreeing the collection times and asking volunteers to cover each table; the committee still decided the membership rules, and he referred a new eligibility question back to them.
listening.zh: Ravi 負責統籌圖書交換，議定收書時間並請義工分別照顧各桌；會員規則仍由委員會決定，他把新資格問題交回委員會。

reply.promptEn: Why was Ravi able to refer the new membership question to the committee?
reply.promptZh: Ravi 為甚麼可以把新會員問題交委員會？

options.en: The committee retained responsibility for the membership rules.
options.zh: 委員會仍負責會員規則。

options.en: He had taken charge of the practical exchange, not of deciding every rule.
options.zh: 他負責實際交換安排，不是決定所有規則。

options.en: The new question fell outside the collection and table arrangements he was coordinating.
options.zh: 新問題不在他統籌的收書與桌位安排範圍。

options.en: Referring the question respected the division of responsibilities already described.
options.zh: 轉交問題，尊重已說明的責任分配。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均解釋政策與實際安排的分工，轉交並非不負責。

scene.promptZh: 小組還沒分配活動統籌，Alex 說願在得到授權後負責，但現在仍在等大家回覆。哪句最準確？

options.en: Alex has offered to take charge of the activity, but the group has not yet agreed the appointment.
options.zh: Alex 已提出願負責活動，但小組尚未議定任命。

options.en: Alex has already been appointed and has set the group’s working arrangements.
options.zh: Alex 已獲任命，也定好小組工作安排。

options.en: Waiting for the group’s reply proves that Alex has refused any responsibility.
options.zh: 等小組回覆，證明 Alex 已拒絕負任何責任。

scene.explanationZh: 提出願意、獲同意及開始安排不同；等待回覆也未表示拒絕。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 take charge of an activity 推出？

options.en: Someone assumes responsibility for organising or managing it.
options.zh: 某人負起統籌或管理它的責任。

options.en: Every related decision now belongs to that person, regardless of the agreed remit.
options.zh: 無論議定範圍如何，每項相關決定現都屬那人。

options.en: The organiser may coordinate tasks carried out by other people.
options.zh: 統籌者可協調由其他人執行的任務。

contrast.explanationZh: 負責有範圍，可分工；不是無限接管。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說 Ravi 既是統籌，就應直接答會員資格，不必問委員會；規則仍由委員會決定。哪句最好？

options.en: He took charge of the exchange arrangements, so he should coordinate the work and refer this rule question to the committee.
options.zh: 他負責交換安排，應統籌工作，並把這項規則問題交委員會。

options.en: He can answer this case according to his own idea of fairness and ask the committee about future cases.
options.zh: 他可按自己認為公平的方式答這次，再就以後個案問委員會。

options.en: The committee’s policy role means Ravi should stop coordinating the tables and collection times too.
options.zh: 委員會負責政策，表示 Ravi 也應停止統籌桌位及收書時間。

dialogue.explanationZh: 保留實際責任並尊重政策權限；不能用個人看法代委員會處理這次政策，也不因需轉交便放棄原責任。

speaking.en: I can take charge of the practical arrangements while checking which decisions still need the group’s agreement.
speaking.zh: 我可負責實際安排，同時查哪些決定仍需小組同意。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把負責範圍及共同決定說清。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友想為親人辦一個小型紀念聚會，事情多卻不想別人替他選音樂或發言者。你願幫聯絡場地及回覆時間，但想先徵求他同意，讓他保留私人內容的決定。用一至兩句英文直接提出幫忙，不擅自接管整場。

examples.en: Would you like me to take charge of the venue enquiries and reply times while you keep the choices about music and speakers? We can agree what I may confirm before I contact anyone.
examples.zh: 你想我負責查場地及回覆時間，而音樂與發言者仍由你選嗎？聯絡任何人前，我們可先議我能確認甚麼。

examples.en: I could take charge of the practical messages if that would help, without taking over the personal decisions. Please tell me which arrangements you want me to handle and which you would rather keep.
examples.zh: 若有幫助，我可負責實際聯絡，不接管私人決定；請告訴我哪些安排想我處理，哪些想自己保留。

writing.selfCheckZh: 先問是否需要，再分可幫聯絡及朋友保留的私人決定；不把想幫忙當已獲全部授權。

takeaways.en: She took charge of the workshop rota and asked each helper to confirm the time they could actually offer.
takeaways.zh: 她負責工作坊輪值表，並請每位幫手確認實際能提供的時間。

takeaways.en: He was ready to take charge of the display setup, but wanted the group to agree the layout before he moved anything.
takeaways.zh: 他願負責佈置展示，但搬任何物件前，希望小組先議定布局。

lessons.titleZh: 像火花般引起興趣或行動

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A friendly challenge can act like a spark for new ideas.

brief.meaningEn: Serve as a small trigger that starts interest, ideas or activity.
brief.meaningZh: 作為一個小觸發點，帶起興趣、想法或活動。
brief.grammar: a question/challenge/experience acts like a spark for + ideas/interest; acted/acting. Explain what begins after the trigger, rather than treat a spark as the whole sustained process.
brief.register: Productive fire-origin simile. It differs in focus from an emotional spark naming a felt connection: this frame identifies something as a trigger for activity or thought.
brief.boundaryZh: 火花可帶開始，不保證之後持續、全部完成或一定成功；需有被引起的反應。
brief.misconceptionZh: 一項提示有用，不表示後續練習、材料及合作都可省；也不把所有興趣都歸單一原因。
brief.outcomeZh: 能連觸發事件到具體新想法，保留後續需要。

listening.promptZh: 問題觸發了甚麼，甚麼仍未做？

options.en: It started ideas for interviews, while identity checks and permission remained to be arranged.
options.zh: 它帶起訪問構思，身分核查及許可仍待安排。

options.en: The interviews had already been completed and approved before the question was asked.
options.zh: 提問前，訪問已完成並獲批准。

options.en: The group decided the photograph contained no questions worth pursuing.
options.zh: 小組判斷照片沒有值得追查的問題。

options.en: Listing possible interviewees confirmed that each person had agreed to participate.
options.zh: 列出可能受訪者，確認每人都已答應參與。

listening.explanationZh: 列訪問構思是開始，未代核身分、許可及完成訪問。
listening.en: The question about who was missing from the photograph acted like a spark for the archive group: members began listing people to interview, though they had not yet checked names or asked anyone for permission.
listening.zh: 「照片裏缺了誰」這問題，像火花般觸發檔案小組；成員開始列想訪問的人，但尚未核名字或徵求任何人許可。

reply.promptEn: Why did the question change the archive group’s discussion?
reply.promptZh: 這問題為甚麼改變檔案小組的討論？

options.en: It led members to think about people they could ask, rather than only describe the visible faces.
options.zh: 它讓成員想可問哪些人，不只描述可見面孔。

options.en: It acted like a spark for new interview ideas by drawing attention to someone absent from the picture.
options.zh: 它讓大家留意照片缺席的人，像火花般引起新訪問構思。

options.en: Members began proposing a way to investigate what the picture left out.
options.zh: 成員開始提出查照片沒呈現之處的方法。

options.en: The question supplied a starting point for further enquiry, even though the checks were unfinished.
options.zh: 問題給進一步查問的起點，雖然核查尚未完成。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均交代開始新構思的具體方向，不把構思當已完成調查。

scene.promptZh: 角色早已寫完完整菜單，之後才看到朋友的一張色卡；色卡令她換封面顏色，卻不是菜單構思的起點。哪句最超出資料？

options.en: The card acted like a spark for all the menu ideas before she began writing them.
options.zh: 她開始寫之前，色卡像火花般引起所有菜單構思。

options.en: The card prompted a later change to the cover colour.
options.zh: 色卡促成稍後封面顏色的改動。

options.en: Her menu ideas were already written before she saw the card.
options.zh: 看到色卡前，她已寫好菜單構思。

scene.explanationZh: 色卡可觸發後來改色，不能倒推成早已完成構思的起點。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 acted like a spark for new ideas 推出？

options.en: Something triggered the beginning of ideas or activity.
options.zh: 某事觸發想法或活動的開始。

options.en: The trigger supplied everything needed to sustain and complete the later work.
options.zh: 觸發點提供了維持及完成後續工作所需的一切。

options.en: The account can show which thought or action began afterwards.
options.zh: 敘述可顯示之後開始了哪項想法或行動。

contrast.explanationZh: 開始的火花不是全部後續條件。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友想名單一列好便直接公開訪問計劃，當各人已答應；目前只有構思。哪句最好？

options.en: The question acted like a spark for ideas, but we need to check the names and ask permission before announcing people as participants.
options.zh: 問題像火花般帶起構思，但公布誰參加前，需先核名字及問許可。

options.en: Publish the proposed names first and ask permission only if someone objects afterwards.
options.zh: 先公開擬議名字，有人之後反對才問許可。

options.en: Ask only the member who suggested the interviews, rather than the people whose participation we would announce.
options.zh: 只問提出訪問的成員，不問將被宣布參加的人。

dialogue.explanationZh: 肯定構思已開始，同時核查並徵求參加者許可；不能先公開，也不能只問提議人代替參加者。

speaking.en: The small question acted like a spark for our enquiry, but the ideas still needed careful checking and willing participants.
speaking.zh: 小問題像火花般帶起我們的查問，但構思仍需仔細核查及自願參加者。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把開始觸發與持續工作分開。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫給朋友的觀展短信。一件裂開後修補的碗讓你突然想試把舊衣裂口變成設計細節，而非直接丟掉；你還未做成，想先拿一小塊布試縫，不說藝術品已替你解決所有修補問題。用一至兩句英文描述這個跨媒介構思及下一步。

examples.en: The repaired bowl acted like a spark for an idea about turning a tear in old clothing into part of the design. I want to try a few stitches on a small piece of fabric before deciding how to repair the whole garment.
examples.zh: 修補的碗像火花般，讓我想到把舊衣裂口變設計一部分；決定怎修整件衣前，我想先在小布片試幾針。

examples.en: Seeing the repaired bowl acts like a spark for a sewing experiment, not a finished solution. I will test the idea on a scrap first and see what the fabric can actually hold.
examples.zh: 看到修補的碗，像火花般帶起縫紉試驗構思，並非完成方案；我會先在碎布試，看看布料實際能承受甚麼。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把觀展意象連到不同媒介的具體試驗，保留尚未完成及材料需測，不把靈感當全部技術已會。

takeaways.en: The child’s question acted like a spark for a new ending, and the writer began trying a different final conversation.
takeaways.zh: 孩子問題像火花般引起新結尾構思，作者開始試不同的最後對話。

takeaways.en: The unexpected colour pairing acts like a spark for her sketches, though she chooses which ideas to develop afterwards.
takeaways.zh: 意外配色像火花般帶起她的速寫構思，之後她仍會選哪些想法繼續發展。

lessons.titleZh: 使人警覺、認真注意起來

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A short deadline sometimes wakes people up.

brief.meaningEn: Make people become alert to something or begin taking it seriously.
brief.meaningZh: 讓人警覺到某事，或開始認真看待。
brief.grammar: wake someone up; wake people up to + problem/fact. The person comes between wake and up in these transitive examples. This figurative use does not imply anyone was physically asleep.
brief.register: Common waking metaphor for attention and awareness. Urgency may prompt action but can also add pressure; the effect needs context.
brief.boundaryZh: 讓人留意不等於已解決問題，也不表示之前一定懶惰或睡着；要說新注意到甚麼。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能把限期逼近當資料已核，也不以行動較慢推個人態度。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把提示連到注意及查證，保留實際支援和結果未定。

listening.promptZh: 他們注意到甚麼，結果仍怎樣？

options.en: They noticed the permission gap and asked for clarification, which was still pending.
options.zh: 他們留意到許可缺口並查問，回覆仍待收到。

options.en: The photographer had approved every use before the group noticed the missing note.
options.zh: 小組留意缺記錄前，攝影者已批准所有用途。

options.en: The group used the deadline to finish only the title and left the permission question unasked.
options.zh: 小組只利用限期完成標題，沒有問許可。

options.en: They asked a fellow group member to approve the photograph instead of asking the photographer.
options.zh: 他們請組員代為批准照片，沒有問攝影者。

listening.explanationZh: woke up to 指留意許可缺口；他們已問攝影者而非組員，回覆仍未到，不是已獲批准。
listening.en: The short deadline woke the group up to a missing permission note: they stopped polishing the title and asked the photographer what could be shared, but the answer had not arrived when the meeting ended.
listening.zh: 短限期讓小組警覺缺了一份許可記錄：他們暫停修標題，問攝影者哪些可分享，但會議結束時尚未收到答案。

reply.promptEn: Why did the deadline change what the group attended to?
reply.promptZh: 限期為甚麼改變小組留意的事情？

options.en: They realised a permission note was missing before they could share the photograph.
options.zh: 他們發現分享照片前，還缺一份許可記錄。

options.en: It woke them up to an unresolved permission question, so they asked the photographer directly.
options.zh: 它讓他們警覺未解許可問題，所以直接問攝影者。

options.en: The urgent timing drew attention away from polishing the title and towards a needed check.
options.zh: 時間迫切，把注意從修標題轉到必要查核。

options.en: They began taking the missing note seriously rather than assume it could wait until after sharing.
options.zh: 他們開始認真看待缺記錄，不再假定可分享後才處理。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均解釋注意到必要查核，不把留意問題當已得到答案。

scene.promptZh: 小說人物在鬧鐘響後睜眼起床，沒有新認識或改變看法的描述。哪句最能區分用義？

options.en: The alarm woke her up literally; this account does not yet describe new awareness of a problem.
options.zh: 鬧鐘實際叫醒她；這敘述尚未描寫對問題的新警覺。

options.en: The alarm has made her understand an unresolved problem at work.
options.zh: 鬧鐘已讓她明白工作上一個未解問題。

options.en: She stayed asleep and the sound prompted only the people in the next room to act.
options.zh: 她仍睡着，聲音只促使隔壁的人行動。

scene.explanationZh: 本例有實際起床，未說新認識；跟本課警覺問題的比喻不同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能由 a deadline woke people up 的比喻推出？

options.en: People began paying serious attention to something.
options.zh: 大家開始認真留意某事。

options.en: The practical problem they noticed has already been solved.
options.zh: 他們留意到的實際問題已解決。

options.en: The account should show what they noticed or did differently.
options.zh: 敘述應顯示他們注意或改做甚麼。

contrast.explanationZh: 注意及開始行動不是問題已解。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友想限期一到便公開照片，說小組既已「警覺」就不用再等許可；回覆仍未到。哪句最好？

options.en: The deadline woke us up to the permission gap, not to an answer; we need the photographer’s reply before deciding what to share.
options.zh: 限期讓我們警覺許可缺口，不是給了答案；決定分享甚麼前，需等攝影者回覆。

options.en: We noticed the issue in time, so the missing reply no longer affects what we may publish.
options.zh: 我們及時留意問題，所以缺回覆已不影響可公開甚麼。

options.en: Keep polishing the title and leave the permission question until after people have seen the photograph.
options.zh: 繼續修標題，等大家看過照片才談許可。

dialogue.explanationZh: 警覺應帶來必要查核，不把注意代許可，也不把關鍵問題留到公開後。

speaking.en: The conversation woke me up to the missing information, but I still needed to ask rather than fill the gap with a guess.
speaking.zh: 對話讓我警覺缺資料，但我仍需查問，不用猜測填補。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分警覺、查問與已得答案。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替學生環境展寫一段圖說，一張河邊垃圾照片讓你開始關心沿岸使用方式；但只有一處、一日的照片，不能判全河情況或指責某類人。用一至兩句英文，說它帶起的警覺及你想再了解甚麼。

examples.en: This photograph can wake people up to the litter at this riverside spot, but it cannot tell us what happens along the whole river. I would like to compare other places and ask how the area is used before assigning blame.
examples.zh: 這照片可讓人警覺河邊此處的垃圾，但不能告訴我們整條河的情況；歸責前，我想比較其他地點，並問大家怎使用這區。

examples.en: The image woke me up to a question about how we share the riverbank, not to a complete explanation of who left the rubbish. It gives me a reason to investigate beyond this one place and day.
examples.zh: 圖像讓我警覺大家怎共用河岸的問題，不是給了誰留垃圾的完整解釋；它讓我想查這一處、這一天以外的情況。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把照片當注意問題的起點，限定觀察範圍並提出比較及查問，不用一張照片概括全河或指控某類人。

takeaways.en: The unexpected question woke the team up to a gap in the visitor guide, and they asked newcomers to test that section.
takeaways.zh: 意外問題讓小組警覺訪客指南的缺口，他們便請新人測試那部分。

takeaways.en: The former pupil’s letter woke the team up to the missing names in the school display, and they asked the archive for the original register.
takeaways.zh: 舊生的信令小組警覺校內展示漏了名字，他們便向檔案室查原名冊。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Winning at all costs can ruin a friendship.

brief.meaningEn: Seek victory regardless of damage or unacceptable consequences.
brief.meaningZh: 不理損害或不可接受的後果，一心求勝。
brief.grammar: winning at all costs; want/try to win at all costs. This is stronger than working hard or caring about a result: the context shows what the person is willing to sacrifice.
brief.register: Established cost metaphor. The costs can be trust, fairness, health or relationships rather than money.
brief.boundaryZh: 想贏不等於不擇手段；要有願犧牲甚麼的線索，也不由一次落敗判一個人全部態度。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可認真競賽而保留公平、休息及他人界限，不必在毫不在乎與不惜代價之間二選一。
brief.outcomeZh: 能按具體行為分清投入競賽與壓過重要原則的求勝。

listening.promptZh: Lee 反對甚麼，仍想保留甚麼？

options.en: He rejected sacrificing an agreed rule for advantage while still wanting a serious contest.
options.zh: 他反對為優勢犧牲議定規則，仍想認真競賽。

options.en: He wanted to stop all competition because he no longer cared about playing.
options.zh: 他已不在乎玩遊戲，想停止所有競賽。

options.en: He supported cancelling the pause only when it would disadvantage the other side.
options.zh: 只要取消暫停會令對手吃虧，他便支持。

options.en: Both teams had already agreed to remove the pause before the organiser raised it.
options.zh: 統籌提出前，兩隊已同意取消暫停。

listening.explanationZh: 反對的是為贏而破約，不是反對認真競賽；規則尚未被雙方更改。
listening.en: When the game organiser suggested ignoring an agreed pause because it might help the other team, Lee objected to winning at all costs; he wanted a serious match without breaking the rule both sides had accepted.
listening.zh: 遊戲統籌提議不理雙方議定的暫停，因它可能幫到對手，Lee 反對不惜代價求勝；他想認真比賽，但不破壞雙方接受的規則。

reply.promptEn: Why did Lee object to the organiser’s suggestion?
reply.promptZh: Lee 為甚麼反對統籌建議？

options.en: Both sides had accepted the pause as part of the rules.
options.zh: 雙方已把暫停接受為規則的一部分。

options.en: Winning at all costs would sacrifice an agreement just to deny the other team a benefit.
options.zh: 不惜代價求勝，會只為不讓對手得益而犧牲協議。

options.en: He wanted competition to remain consistent with the terms both teams had agreed.
options.zh: 他想競賽仍符合兩隊議定的條件。

options.en: Taking the match seriously did not require abandoning the agreed pause.
options.zh: 認真比賽，不需要放棄議定暫停。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均說明規則及公平承諾，不把反對違約當不想競賽。

scene.promptZh: 球員加練、分析過去失誤，也接受對手休息及裁判規則；資料沒說他願用欺騙或傷害換勝利。哪句最超出所述？

options.en: His extra practice proves that he is trying to win at all costs.
options.zh: 額外練習，證明他正不惜一切代價求勝。

options.en: He is working seriously while accepting limits on how the contest is played.
options.zh: 他認真努力，同時接受競賽方式的界限。

options.en: The account distinguishes preparation from breaking agreed rules.
options.zh: 敘述把準備與破壞議定規則分開。

scene.explanationZh: 努力想贏，未證願犧牲原則；需看可接受哪些代價。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 winning at all costs？

options.en: A player accepts unfair damage to others in order to secure victory.
options.zh: 球員為勝利，接受對別人造成不公平損害。

options.en: A competitor tries hard but refuses an advantage that would break the agreed rules.
options.zh: 參賽者努力，但拒絕違反議定規則的優勢。

options.en: The desire to win takes priority over a relationship the person harms.
options.zh: 求勝欲壓過當事人正在損害的關係。

contrast.explanationZh: 願維持原則的競爭，不等於不惜代價。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說 Lee 堅持暫停就是不夠投入；你想分清重視勝負與破約。哪句最好？

options.en: He wants a serious match without winning at all costs; keeping the agreed rule is compatible with trying hard.
options.zh: 他想認真比賽，但不願不惜代價求勝；守議定規則與努力可以並存。

options.en: To show commitment, he should accept whichever rule change gives his own team an advantage.
options.zh: 要顯投入，他應接受任何令己隊有利的改規。

options.en: If he keeps the pause, he should stop preparing because the result no longer matters to him.
options.zh: 若保留暫停，他就應停止準備，因結果已不重要。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可投入並守界限，不把承諾等同只選己方優勢，也不推他不在乎結果。

speaking.en: I want to win, but not to win at all costs by breaking the agreement that made the contest fair.
speaking.zh: 我想贏，但不願破壞令競賽公平的協議，不惜代價求勝。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把認真競賽與願付的代價分開。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：小說人物發現自己參賽草稿用了一段朋友未同意公開的私人回憶，截止將到。她決定先撤下那段，若趕不及便不交，而不以可能得獎合理化使用。用一至兩句第一人稱獨白，寫出她仍重視作品但拒絕的代價。

examples.en: Winning at all costs would mean using your private memory without permission, and I am not willing to do that. I will remove the passage, even if I cannot finish an entry by the deadline.
examples.zh: 不惜代價求勝，就要未經許可使用你的私人回憶，我不願這樣；我會撤下那段，即使未能在限期前完成參賽稿。

examples.en: I care about this story, but winning at all costs cannot be my reason for exposing something you trusted me with. I would rather miss this entry than keep the private passage without your agreement.
examples.zh: 我重視故事，但不惜代價求勝，不能成為公開你信任我才告知之事的理由；我寧願錯過這次參賽，也不未得同意便保留私人段落。

glossary.zh: 你因信任而告訴我的事

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫清拒絕的具體代價及可做決定，保留重視創作；不把想贏當已有他人許可，也不宣告此後永不參賽。

takeaways.en: The captain rejected winning at all costs when a proposed shortcut would have broken the team’s agreement with its opponents.
takeaways.zh: 建議捷徑會違反與對手協議時，隊長拒絕不惜代價求勝。

takeaways.en: She could enjoy the challenge without trying to win at all costs or treating a friend’s disappointment as irrelevant.
takeaways.zh: 她可享受挑戰，不必不惜代價求勝，也不把朋友失望當無關。

lessons.titleZh: 改過自新、重新做人做事

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: After the warning, he decided to turn over a new leaf.

brief.meaningEn: Begin behaving in a better or more responsible way after a previous pattern of conduct.
brief.meaningZh: 在以往某種行為模式之後，開始以較好或更負責的方式行事。
brief.grammar: turn over a new leaf; turned/turning. Intending to change, beginning new behaviour and sustaining it are different stages.
brief.register: Established fresh-start idiom, not a literal page or plant leaf. Identify the behaviour rather than use the phrase as a judgement of a person’s entire worth.
brief.boundaryZh: 重新開始不抹去已造成的影響，也不憑一句承諾證明長期改好；需具體行動及時間。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可承認首次改變而保留仍待建立的信任，不要求一次行為代表永不再錯。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述行為改變的起點、補救及仍需實踐的部分。

options.en: He tried a different way to participate and asked how it affected other speakers.
options.zh: 他嘗試不同參與方式，並問它對其他發言者有何影響。

options.en: He announced an intention but did not attend or change his behaviour at the next meeting.
options.zh: 他只宣布意願，下次沒有到場或改變行為。

options.en: He asked others to stop speaking so he would not need to wait.
options.zh: 他叫別人停止發言，讓自己不用等。

options.en: He had used the waiting arrangement throughout, so there was no earlier interruption pattern.
options.zh: 他一直都有等待，之前沒有打斷別人的模式。

listening.explanationZh: 記問題、等停頓及問影響，是已試行的新行為；未證長期，但不是只有口號。
listening.en: After repeatedly interrupting, Tom decided to turn over a new leaf: at the next meeting he wrote down his question and waited for a pause, then asked others whether the new arrangement gave them enough space.
listening.zh: 屢次打斷別人後，Tom 決定改過；下次會議他記下問題，等到停頓才問，再詢問大家新安排是否給足表達空間。

reply.promptEn: Why do you say Tom has begun changing his meeting behaviour?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼說 Tom 已開始改會議行為？

options.en: He waited for a pause instead of repeatedly interrupting.
options.zh: 他等待停頓，不再一再打斷。

options.en: He began to turn over a new leaf by recording his question and checking how others experienced the change.
options.zh: 他記問題並查別人對改變的感受，開始改過。

options.en: The next meeting contained an observable alternative to the earlier interruptions.
options.zh: 下次會議中，出現了可觀察、不同於先前打斷的做法。

options.en: He made room for other speakers and asked whether the new arrangement helped.
options.zh: 他留空間給其他發言者，並問新安排有沒有幫助。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均以已試行為說起點，不用一句決心當長期紀錄。

scene.promptZh: 人物說決定改掉遲交借物，尚未到下一次歸還日，也未看見之後怎做。哪句最準確？

options.en: She wants to turn over a new leaf, but the account has not yet shown how she follows that intention.
options.zh: 她想改過，但敘述尚未顯示之後怎實踐。

options.en: Her statement confirms that she has already returned the next borrowed item on time.
options.zh: 她的話確認下一件借物已準時還。

options.en: Because there is no later record yet, her wish to change must be insincere.
options.zh: 還沒有之後紀錄，所以想改的意願必定不真誠。

scene.explanationZh: 意願可真誠，但仍待行動；不把尚未發生當已準時，也不因此斷言不真誠。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 turned over a new leaf 推出？

options.en: A person has begun a positive change in behaviour.
options.zh: 某人已開始正面的行為改變。

options.en: Every earlier consequence has disappeared and trust needs no further repair.
options.zh: 先前每項後果已消失，信任不需再修補。

options.en: The context should identify what behaviour changed.
options.zh: 情境應指出哪種行為改變。

contrast.explanationZh: 新開始與補救舊影響不同，信任仍需時間及行動。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴要因 Tom 一次等停頓，就保證他之後都不會打斷；你想肯定起步但不誇大。哪句最好？

options.en: He has begun to turn over a new leaf; let us recognise this meeting’s change and keep checking how the arrangement works.
options.zh: 他已開始改過；肯定這次會議的改變，也繼續看安排怎運作吧。

options.en: One good meeting means there is no need to hear from the people he used to interrupt.
options.zh: 一次好會議，表示不用再聽曾被打斷的人說甚麼。

options.en: The written questions are enough to judge the arrangement; we do not need to ask whether others had space to speak.
options.zh: 單看寫下的問題已夠判斷安排，不需問其他人是否有發言空間。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可肯定實際起點並持續問效果，不以一次保證長期，也不以筆記代其他人的實際發言空間。

speaking.en: I want to turn over a new leaf, and I know I need to show that in what I do rather than ask people to forget the earlier harm.
speaking.zh: 我想改過，也知道需用行動顯示，不是要求大家忘記以前的影響。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分新的起點與仍需補救。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：故事人物曾轉傳未核實的消息，令朋友被誤會。她現在知道資料錯，想先向收到消息的人更正，再約定日後未核便不轉，並接受朋友未必立刻信任。用一至兩句第一人稱英文寫她的承諾，包含補救，不宣告信任已恢復。

examples.en: I want to turn over a new leaf, beginning by correcting the false message with the people I sent it to. I will check before passing on another claim, without expecting you to trust me again immediately.
examples.zh: 我想改過，先向收到我轉傳消息的人更正錯誤；之後轉傳前會核查，不期望你立即再信我。

examples.en: Turning over a new leaf means I must repair what I spread, not only promise to be more careful. I will send the correction and stop forwarding unverified claims, while leaving you time to decide what trust is possible.
examples.zh: 改過意味着我要補救已傳開的事，不只承諾更小心；我會發更正，不再轉未核主張，也讓你有時間決定能信我多少。

glossary.en: the people I sent it to
check before passing on another claim
glossary.zh: 轉傳另一主張前先核查

writing.selfCheckZh: 把改過連到先更正既有影響及之後查核，留朋友的時間與選擇；不要求對方因一句承諾便恢復信任。

takeaways.en: She turned over a new leaf by returning borrowed materials when promised and asking before changing the collection date.
takeaways.zh: 她按承諾歸還借物，改領取日前先問，開始改過。

takeaways.en: He hoped to turn over a new leaf, but his apology still needed to be followed by a different way of handling the next disagreement.
takeaways.zh: 他希望改過，但道歉之後，仍需以不同方式處理下次分歧。

lessons.titleZh: 讓生活回到自己選定的軌道

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: For her, getting life back on track began with a simple routine.

brief.meaningEn: Return one’s life towards a more stable or intended course after disruption.
brief.meaningZh: 生活受打亂後，逐步回到較穩定或自己原想走的方向。
brief.grammar: get/getting/got one’s life back on track; explain what the person wants to recover, rather than impose one universal life plan. A beginning can be described without claiming complete recovery.
brief.register: Established journey metaphor. Stability, routine, relationships or meaningful activity may be the intended direction; outward productivity alone does not define it.
brief.boundaryZh: 回軌可依當事人的目標，不必回原來全部安排，也不表示困難已全解。
brief.misconceptionZh: 日常小改動可有作用，但不能由一次行動宣布整個人生已恢復；也不替別人定唯一正常路線。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體而自選的生活目標描述恢復，保留尚未穩定部分。

listening.promptZh: 她恢復的是甚麼，還有甚麼未完成？

options.en: She was rebuilding valued routines while some practical moving tasks remained.
options.zh: 她正重建重視的日常，部分搬家工作仍未完成。

options.en: All unpacking had finished before she could begin either arrangement.
options.zh: 她先拆完所有箱，才開始任何一項安排。

options.en: She had abandoned contact with her sister to concentrate entirely on unpacking.
options.zh: 她放棄聯絡姐姐，只專注拆箱。

options.en: A regular library visit was someone else’s imposed plan, which she said she did not value.
options.zh: 定期去圖書館是別人強加，她說自己不重視。

listening.explanationZh: 恢復她自選的日常與未拆箱並存，不等於所有事已好，也非放棄關係或被強加目標。
listening.en: For Noor, getting life back on track after the move began with a regular library visit and a weekly call to her sister; she still had boxes to unpack, but those two arrangements restored parts of the routine she valued.
listening.zh: 搬家後，對 Noor 而言，讓生活回軌先從定期到圖書館及每周致電姐姐開始；她仍有箱未拆，但兩項安排恢復了她重視的部分日常。

reply.promptEn: Why did Noor begin with the library visit and the call?
reply.promptZh: Noor 為甚麼先做圖書館探訪及通話安排？

options.en: They restored activities and contact that she personally valued.
options.zh: 它們恢復她個人重視的活動及聯絡。

options.en: Getting life back on track meant rebuilding those familiar parts, not waiting until every box was empty.
options.zh: 對她，生活回軌是重建這些熟悉部分，不是等每箱都清空。

options.en: The arrangements gave her week some shape after the disruption of moving.
options.zh: 搬家打亂日常後，安排讓一周重新有些規律。

options.en: She could begin recovering something meaningful while the practical work continued.
options.zh: 實際工作繼續時，她仍可開始找回有意義的事。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均以她重視的日常解釋起點，不替她定唯一整體恢復標準。

scene.promptZh: 朋友認為只有回全職工作才算回軌，但故事中的父親選擇先恢復跟兒子的每周散步，並說這對自己很重要；工作安排仍在考慮。哪句最謹慎？

options.en: Getting his life back on track can include that valued connection, while the work decision remains open.
options.zh: 讓生活回軌，可包括這項重視的聯繫，工作決定仍未定。

options.en: The weekly walk confirms that he has already accepted a full-time job.
options.zh: 每周散步，確認他已接受全職工作。

options.en: Until he chooses full-time work, no part of his routine can have become more stable.
options.zh: 未選全職工作前，他日常任何部分都不可能較穩定。

scene.explanationZh: 回軌要連他本人重視的生活，不把散步當已定工作，也不抹去部分穩定。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只憑 get life back on track 推出？

options.en: Someone is moving towards a more stable or intended life direction.
options.zh: 某人正朝較穩定或原想走的生活方向前進。

options.en: They must restore every detail of the old routine, regardless of what they now want.
options.zh: 無論現在想甚麼，他們都必須恢復舊日常每項細節。

options.en: The context should explain which direction or routine matters to that person.
options.zh: 情境應解釋哪種方向或日常對當事人重要。

contrast.explanationZh: 回到有意義方向，不等於照搬舊安排全部細節。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友要替 Noor 加滿每天活動，認為越忙越能回軌；她只先選兩項安排。哪句最好？

options.en: Let her say what getting life back on track means for her; the two chosen routines need not become a full timetable of our making.
options.zh: 讓她說生活回軌對自己是甚麼；兩項自選日常，不需變成我們替她排滿的時間表。

options.en: Add the other activities first and ask which she values only after the week is full.
options.zh: 先加其他活動，排滿一周後才問她重視哪些。

options.en: The two routines show that her whole week is already settled, so no further choices need discussion.
options.zh: 兩項日常顯示整周安排已完全穩定，之後的選擇都不用再談。

dialogue.explanationZh: 按她的目標及選擇協助，不用忙碌程度代她決定，也不把兩項已定安排擴成全部選擇都已完成。

speaking.en: Getting my life back on track means choosing which routines and relationships I want to rebuild, not simply filling every hour.
speaking.zh: 讓生活回軌，是選想重建哪些日常與關係，不只是把每小時排滿。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說當事人想恢復的生活方向。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：角色多年按別人的升職目標生活，工作仍有條理，卻覺得失去自己想做的事。她想重拾每周為自己寫一頁故事，不求發表，先向朋友說明這也是自己想回到的方向，而不宣告應立即辭職。用一至兩句第一人稱英文寫她的說法。

examples.en: Getting my life back on track is not only about keeping my work organised; I also want time for a story that belongs to me. I will begin with one private page each week, without making publication the condition for writing.
examples.zh: 讓生活回軌，不只是把工作安排好，我也想有時間寫屬自己的故事；我會先每周私下寫一頁，不以發表作寫作條件。

examples.en: I want to get my life back on track by bringing my own writing into it again, not by taking on another promotion goal. One page for myself each week would be a beginning, while I think about the larger choices.
examples.zh: 我想重新把自己的寫作帶回生活，讓生活回軌，不是再接一個升職目標；思考較大選擇時，先每周為自己寫一頁，就是起點。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以角色自己的創作方向說回軌，提出小而真實的開始；不把工作有序等同所有意義，也不從想寫作直接跳到未決的辭職。

takeaways.en: She began to get her life back on track by restoring contact with the friends she had missed, while leaving other decisions open.
takeaways.zh: 她恢復跟掛念朋友的聯絡，開始讓生活回軌，其他決定仍未定。

takeaways.en: Getting life back on track after the disruption took several small changes, not a single promise that everything was normal again.
takeaways.zh: 生活受打亂後，回軌需幾項小改動，不是一句承諾便說一切正常。
